sentences.text:
Claim case filed by respondent No. 1, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.
86,507/- alongwith interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of claim case and liability was fastened over driver and owner and Insurance Company jointly and severally.
2. It is the submission of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that learned Claims Tribunal erred in passing the impugned award.

It is submitted that though the Claimant/respondent No. 1 has filed the claim case stating to be the Conductor of the truck; however, in evidence he could not disclose the name of owner of the truck and further no documents have been filed which can show that he was Conductor in the Truck.
Interestingly, it is also submitted that there is no requirement of Conductor in a truck as Conductor is required in a passenger vehicle for distributing tickets after collecting money.
Thus, it is clear that after the accident, story was cooked that he was an employee on the truck; whereas, it is clear that he was travelling in the truck in the capacity of passenger.
3. None appeared on behalf of the respondents to contest the case.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
5.
Appeal is filed by the Insurance Company on the ground of non- liability.
6. Admittedly, from the statement of respondent No. 1 and his cross- examination it is clear that he was not an employee on the vehicle.
As even he was not knowing the name of owner of the vehicle and what article was the vehicle carrying on the date of accident.
Further he claimed himself to be the Conductor on the truck, whereas, no conductor is required on truck (Tata 407) and thus, he was travelling in the capacity of a Passenger.

It is also not in dispute that the respondent No. 2 has caused the accident by driving the vehicle Tata 407 bearing registration No. MP06GA0172 negligently and in this accident, respondent No. 1 sustained grievous hurts.
It is also an admitted facts that at the time of accident, the above vehicle was insured with the appellant/Insurance Company.
The vehicle in question is a goods carrying vehicle and is insured as such.
Hence, carrying of passengers by this vehicle is not allowed.
The risk of passenger be it fare paying or gratuitous is not covered under the Insurance Policy.

7. Further during pendency of claim case the appellant has taken objection regarding non possessing of valid permit and driving licence; however, from the impugned award it is clear that said objections have been overruled on flimsy grounds without considering the fact that such documents have also not been produced on behalf of owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

8. As such, Insurance Company cannot be held liable for payment of compensation amount and further since injured was not a third party and owner, driver and Insurance Company of vehicle to which the vehicle in which respondent No. 1 was travelling and collided with not being made parties,
in such matter doctrine of pay and recover cannot be applied and owner of the vehicle alone is liable to pay damages to the claimant, as accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle.
If any amount is paid by the insurance company to the claimant, the insurance company is entitled to get back the same.
